checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Compact conical tubing coiled into oval shape, noticeably shorter than a trumpet.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The instruments appear to be standard Bb trumpets with cylindrical tubing sections, not the predominantly conical bore of a cornet. They do not look 'noticeably shorter' than a standard trumpet; they look like standard trumpets.
The bells are flared and oriented generally forward/downward as expected for upright display.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tubing diameter gradually increases from mouthpiece to bell.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Trumpets have cylindrical tubing for most of their length before the bell flare. A gradual increase from mouthpiece is characteristic of a cornet or flugelhorn, which is not what is depicted here.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three piston valves arranged vertically on top with finger buttons.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All five instruments clearly show three vertical piston valves with buttons.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Cup-shaped detachable mouthpiece inserted into leadpipe.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Mouthpieces are visible at the top of the leadpipes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Finger hooks and thumb ring present for grip.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Thumb rings and pinky hooks are visible on the valve blocks and bell braces.
The instruments are clearly golden-yellow lacquered brass.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Valve casings are cylindrical with visible seam lines.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bell rims appear to have the standard rolled wire edge construction.

artifact_observations.location: Valve clusters and tubing intersections (center instruments)
artifact_observations.reasoning: The mechanical complexity of the valve slides and tuning slides is simplified or melted. On the middle instruments, individual tubes seem to fuse together or terminate abruptly without logical connection to the valve block. The geometry of the water keys and slide receivers is vague or missing.
The reflections on the bells are somewhat generic and repetitive, lacking the specific distortion one would expect from a complex studio environment, though this is minor.
